items.video_title: Kia Picanto AC Suddenly Stopped? Evaporator Leakage Issue & Solution!”
items.video_description:
If your Kia Picanto’s AC suddenly stops working and you suspect an evaporator leakage, here’s what you should check:

Possible Causes & Solutions
 Evaporator Coil Leakage
 If the evaporator has a leak, the AC gas (refrigerant) slowly escapes, causing the AC to stop cooling.
 To confirm the leak, perform a UV Dye Test or a Nitrogen Pressure Test.
 If the leak is confirmed, replacing the evaporator coil is the best solution, as repairs usually don’t last long.
 Low Refrigerant Pressure
 If the evaporator is leaking, the refrigerant level will drop, and the compressor might not engage.
 Recharge the AC only after fixing the leak, otherwise, the gas will escape again.
 Compressor Protection Mode
 Some modern cars have a safety feature that shuts down the AC system when the refrigerant level is too low to prevent compressor damage.
 Fix the leak, refill the refrigerant, and reset the system if needed.
 Cabin Moisture or Foul Smell
 If there’s a bad smell or fogging on the windshield, it could indicate evaporator leakage.
 This often happens when the evaporator coil corrodes over time.

What to Do?
 Visit a professional AC technician to inspect and confirm the issue.
 If the evaporator is leaking, replacement is usually the best option.
 After replacing, ensure proper vacuuming and refrigerant refilling for optimal AC performance.

If your AC is not cooling and only blowing warm air, don’t rush to recharge the system or replace expensive parts just yet. One of the most common and often overlooked causes is a simple electrical issue – a blown fuse or a faulty relay for the AC compressor.

items.video_title: How to check transmission fluid level in Kia Sportage - no dipstick!
items.video_description:
If you're looking for a transmission fluid dipstick in your Kia Sportage, you might be surprised to learn that modern models use a sealed transmission system, meaning checking the fluid level is not as simple as pulling out a dipstick. In this video, I will guide you through the correct procedure to check the automatic transmission fluid (ATF) level in a Kia Sportage.

🔧 What You’ll Learn in This Video:
✔️ When and why you should check the transmission fluid level.
✔️ How to safely lift the vehicle for an accurate reading.
✔️ Step-by-step instructions for checking the ATF level.
✔️ Proper fluid specifications and torque values.

⚠️ Important: Checking the transmission fluid is not part of regular maintenance unless you suspect a leak or experience shifting issues.

📌 Tools & Materials Needed:
✅ Kia-approved SP-IV ATF fluid
✅ Ratchet
✅ Torque wrench (4.9 to 5.9 N·m or 3.6 to 4.3 lb·ft)
✅ Infrared thermometer or scan tool
✅ Jack stands (to lift all four wheels)

👨‍🔧 Step-by-Step Process:
1️⃣ Ensure the vehicle is on a level surface.
2️⃣ Remove the under-engine cover to access the fluid check plug.
3️⃣ Open the ATF filler bolt and add 700 ml of fluid.
4️⃣ Start the engine and warm up the transmission to 50-60°C (122-140°F).
5️⃣ Shift gears to distribute the fluid evenly.
6️⃣ Remove the fluid check plug while the engine is running.
7️⃣ Adjust the fluid level as needed.
8️⃣ Reinstall all components and secure everything properly.

This guide applies to 4th-generation Kia Sportage (QL, 2016-2021) and other models with sealed transmissions.

📢 Let me know in the comments if you have any questions!
